units.title: Statement: contract days 2 to 3 (ref GLS-KH-0001-D03)
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Statement. Reference: GLS-KH-0001-D03. Period: contract days 2 to 3. Status: settlements recorded. Itemised liabilities, payments and balances are shown on the wages page of your Journal, which is the authoritative record. Rates unchanged: $300.00 per active employee-day. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Notice: liabilities past due (ref GLS-KH-0001-A01)
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Arrears notice. Reference: GLS-KH-0001-A01. Status: one or more employee-day liabilities on this site account are unpaid. Order of payment: oldest due first. Note: a liability left unpaid after its due day closes may result in the employee leaving the contract. Partial payments do not move a due date. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Leaver processed (ref GLS-KH-0001-L01)
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Leaver notice. Reference: GLS-KH-0001-L01. Status: an employee record on this site account has been closed. Final liabilities, if any, remain payable and are shown on the wages page of your Journal. No further day rate will accrue for the closed record. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Your policy renewal is coming up
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Dear policyholder, your Lyle Mutual vehicle and personal cover (policy LM-44817-V) is due for renewal at the end of next month. There's nothing you need to do right now. We'll send your renewal documents in good time, and if your details haven't changed, your cover will continue automatically. Peace of mind, without the paperwork.

units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Did you know? Many of our customers save money by adding a second vehicle or a home policy to their account. Small print: cover is subject to the terms in your policy booklet. Vehicles left unattended for extended periods, including at ferry terminals or remote sites, may be subject to conditions. Please check your booklet or call us before a long absence.

units.title: Day 3: a few things
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Morning. A few things:
- The Met Office is forecasting fog over the Sound from tomorrow, possibly for several days. The supply boat runs in fog, but slowly, and the skipper decides.
- If there's anything you'll need in the next week, order it today rather than tomorrow.
- The first full Payroll statement is out. Please check it against your own figures.
Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Fog season is here! Be seen, stay snug
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Fog season is here, and Camp Supply has you covered! This week only: high-visibility vests in three sizes (all of them yellow), reflective tape by the metre, and our best-selling flask, which keeps tea hot for a full twelve hours. Perfect for those long grey days when the sun forgets to show up!

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Customer corner! 'I bought the Harbourglow for my allotment shed and now my neighbours ask me to leave it on so they can find their way home.' Thank you, Doreen from Tollinby! We love hearing how our lanterns brighten up your evenings. Send us your stories and you could win a lantern of your own.

units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Top tip: in fog, sound travels further than you think and light travels less far than you hope. Keep a whistle on your jacket, keep your torch batteries warm in an inside pocket, and agree a meeting point before anyone heads out. Stay safe, stay snug, and see you next week! Unsubscribe any time.

units.title: Note from the client
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: You may have had a welcome note from the client's community desk. That's normal; they send one on every job, I gather, and you don't need to do anything with it. As I said, they're very hands-off. If they ever ask for anything specific, which I don't expect, send it to me first and I'll handle it. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Wages on the site account
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: A quick, polite flag: Payroll shows wages outstanding on the site account. I know the first days are tight while the yard gets going and the money comes in behind the work. Please settle the oldest first. Anyone left unpaid past their due day is entitled to leave, and on an island it's a long way to go and find someone else. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Departure
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: I've seen the leaver notice. Sorry, that's never nice, and it's early to be a person down. I'm afraid I can't send a replacement mid-contract, so the work will have to be planned around the people you've got. If there's anything about why they left that I should know, please put it in the day report. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Re: the trade piece
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: The trade piece came out fine. One line, about crews allowing sixty to ninety days for a site that size, caused a small stir upstairs; the directors would like it known that thirty is achievable. I agree with them. It's an ordinary clearance, just a big one. If you see the article, don't let it get into anyone's head. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Fog days
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: One more on the fog, and then I'll stop. If you can't see the end of a felling lane, please don't fell along it. Nobody upstairs will thank you for a day's numbers if they come with an accident report. Foggy days are good for the yard and the fire. Keep people close to camp and close to each other. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Three days in
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Three days in. Thank you for the reports; they're clear and they arrive, which puts you ahead of most site leads I've worked with. I'll send the weekly check-in at the end of the week. Until then, the usual: lanes, yard, fire, wages, and everyone in at a sensible hour. I'm in the office from quarter past seven if anything comes up. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: What's a tree's favourite drink? (Root beer.)
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief. Three days. By now you'll know who on the crew talks in the morning and who talks at night, and which one does neither. Look after that one. Fog's coming, the radio says. The worst fog I ever worked in, we could hear the saws on the next lane like they were in the tent with us and couldn't see our own boots. Strange, how it plays with sound. Anyway. Hal

units.title: Hedge update (you didn't ask)
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Hedge update, since you can't stop me. The man with the well now brings us tea every morning at ten in a teapot shaped like a cottage. My crew think he's adopted us. I think he's checking we haven't touched the well. Both can be true. Give my regards to the trees. The ones still standing. Hal

units.title: costume crisis
units.author: sam
units.text: costume crisis. Second Reed requires a green leotard and a 'reed hat'. nobody knows what a reed hat is. I made one out of a lampshade frame and green crepe paper and Jamie wore it to dinner and wouldn't take it off. it's on the bedpost now. I keep seeing it out of the corner of my eye and thinking there's a very thin person standing there. this is my life now.

units.title: costume crisis
units.author: sam
units.text: costume crisis. Second Reed requires a green leotard and a 'reed hat', and the school's spare leotards have all gone to the Bulrushes, who apparently have a better agent. so I've had to cut up my old green jumper, the one you said made me look like a pea. Jamie looks wonderful in it. I'm told I'm not allowed to come to the dress rehearsal because I 'cry at everything'. fair.

units.title: the dog has a new hobby
units.author: sam
units.text: the dog has a new hobby, which is standing at the back door at about nine every night and barking at the garden. there is nothing in the garden. I've checked with the big torch. he barks for about a minute and then comes back in very pleased, like he's dealt with it. mum says her old dog did the same every autumn. the vet says 'foxes'. anyway it's very loud and Jamie thinks it's hilarious. love, S x

units.title: No need to reply
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello again, sorry. The lady at the Grieve office told me today that there isn't any outgoing mail from the island, only incoming, so you can't reply even if you wanted to. I didn't know that. Please don't feel bad. I'll just write now and then, if that's all right, and if Tomas is around when you read them you could tell him I said hello.

units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Small news for him, if you're passing it on: I finally got the dentist to give me Saturdays off, and the cat has learned to open the cupboard where the treats are, so I've had to put a hair bobble round the handles like a prison. He'll laugh at that. He used to do the same thing to keep me out of his room. Thank you. Ana

units.title: In Gilliver, a view about to change
units.author: courier
units.text: From the harbour wall at Gilliver, Kittering Holm has always looked the same: a long dark back of trees nine kilometres out, green in summer and nearly black in winter. Within a month, if the contract runs to time, it will be bare. Most people in the village say they have never set foot on it, and many say they never wanted to.

units.author: courier
units.text: 'It's the backdrop,' said the owner of the harbour chandlery. 'You stop seeing it. Then somebody tells you it's going and you look at it properly for the first time in twenty years.' He said trade had been 'a bit up' since the clearance began, mainly fuel and rope for the contractor's supply boat, which uses the slipway most mornings.

units.author: courier
units.text: Older residents recalled earlier uses of the island: a fish-curing station at the landing before the Second War, and, before that, a timber camp in the 1890s. 'My grandmother said the timber men came back early and wouldn't talk about it,' one woman said, before adding: 'But she said that about my grandfather and the war, so make of it what you like.'

units.author: courier
units.text: A creel fisherman who works the water off the Holm said he had seen no change in the catch so far, but was keeping an eye on debris. 'There's a clearing by the landing already, and you can hear them working on a still day,' he said. 'Fair play to them. It's hard graft out there, and there's nowhere to go at the end of the day but a camper.'

units.author: courier
units.text: Ardent Vale Holdings, which owns the island, did not respond to further questions about its plans. The council's planning file contains no other application relating to the Holm. Grieve Land Services said the work was 'progressing as expected' and asked that boats keep clear of the landing during supply runs.

units.title: Ferry warns of fog delays as week of mist forecast
units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines has warned passengers to expect slower crossings from tomorrow, with the Met Office forecasting fog over the Sound for several days. The company said crossings would continue to run but at reduced speed, and that the night services were the most likely to be affected.

units.author: courier
units.text: Advection fog is common on the Sound in late autumn, when mild air moves over sea that is still holding its summer warmth. Local weather watchers say this year's conditions look 'textbook'. Last year a similar spell caused delays of up to forty minutes on the Gilliver leg.

units.author: courier
units.text: Passengers are advised to check bulletins before travelling and to allow extra time for connections. The harbour authority at Gilliver said temporary lamps had been placed at the foot of the slipway while permanent lights are repaired.

units.title: Port Ammet library to open later on weeknights
units.author: courier
units.text: Port Ammet's central library will stay open until eight in the evening on weeknights from next month, after a trial last spring found that evening use had doubled. The library said the extra hours would be staffed by moving shifts rather than hiring, and that the study room on the first floor would be heated 'properly, for once'.

units.author: courier
units.text: The longer hours are part of a wider review of the district's libraries, which also covers the branch libraries in Tollinby and Lisle. Library staff in Tollinby said they hoped the review would 'notice' the branch's school groups, which have grown since the new estate was built.

units.author: courier
units.text: The library's local history room, which holds the Marrow Sound History Society's collection, will keep its existing hours. A volunteer said the room's busiest visitors were 'people looking up their houses and people looking up their grandparents, in that order'.

units.title: Travel live: morning roads and crossings
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:00 Good morning. A cold one: minus 2°C in Brackwater and frost on the untreated roads inland. The reservoir bridge has been gritted, the mill road hasn't. Take it gently. Sound Lines crossings are on time and visibility on the Sound is good, for now.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:25 A car has slid into the verge on the mill road just past the Tollinby turn. Nobody hurt, and a passing farmer has already pulled it out, which we're told he did 'without being asked and while finishing a sandwich'. Some mud on the road.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:50 The Brackwater junction lights are stuck on red towards Port Ammet. The council says contractors are aware. Queues back past the reservoir turning, about fifteen minutes. A listener says he has 'learned a lot about the cones'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:20 Lights at Brackwater working again. Meanwhile Sound Lines is warning of slower crossings from tomorrow as fog moves in. The company says it will post updates on its bulletin page and that the night crossings will run 'at a sensible speed'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:50 That's it from the morning travel desk. Roads are drying out as the sun gets on them. Tonight looks milder, with mist forming over the water after dark. If you're driving the coast road late, dipped headlights and patience.

units.title: Overnight: the night workers' phone-in
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Our overnight show's new Thursday phone-in, in which listeners describe the jobs they do while the rest of the Sound sleeps, drew more than forty calls in its first week. Callers included a baker, a hotel laundry worker, a lobster tank checker and a woman who drives the first bus out of the Weyhaven depot.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The show's producer said the idea came from listeners who 'kept apologising for ringing in at three in the morning, as if they'd been caught out of bed'. Many described the same things about night work: the quiet, the people you only ever see in the dark, and the strange satisfaction of finishing a shift as everyone else is waking up.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: One caller, a field recordist from Brackwater, played a short clip of tawny owls down the phone line. The presenter described it as 'the most peaceful thing I have heard on this programme'. The phone-in returns next Thursday from one in the morning.

units.title: Estuary road closures begin: first night 'went smoothly'
units.author: weypost
units.text: The first overnight closure of the estuary road for resurfacing went smoothly, the city council said, with traffic following the signed diversion through the old dock streets. Contractors planed the surface between the container berth roundabout and the Dellow Court junction, and will lay new asphalt tonight.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Residents near the junction said the noise of the planing machines was 'bad, but less bad than we were told'. One shift worker said she had slept through it entirely. Another said the work lights shining into the lower flats were 'like living inside a football ground'.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The council has asked drivers using the diversion to watch for pedestrians on the dock streets, where pavements are narrow and street lighting is patchy. Closures will continue nightly from 20:00 to 06:00 for the next twelve nights.

units.title: Late-night pharmacy rota changes across the city
units.author: weypost
units.text: Weyhaven's late-night pharmacy rota changes from next week, with the estuary road pharmacy taking on two extra evenings and the city-centre branch closing at ten instead of midnight. Health officials said the change reflected where night-time prescriptions were actually being collected.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Shift workers at the port and the distribution park had complained that the city-centre branch was 'a forty-minute bus ride from anyone who works nights'. The new rota puts a pharmacy within walking distance of the estuary road tower blocks on five nights out of seven.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Pharmacists welcomed the change but asked customers to be patient with the inevitable confusion. 'Someone will turn up at the wrong door at eleven at night with a prescription,' said one. 'They always do. We'll point them the right way.'

units.title: Chainsaw certification changes: what operators need to know
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Changes to chainsaw operator certification come into effect at the start of next year, the industry training board has confirmed. Operators holding older tickets will need a short refresher assessment within three years, covering felling in difficult conditions, windblown timber and working alone.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The 'working alone' module has drawn the most comment. Remote sites, the board says, account for a growing share of serious incidents, often because help is hours away rather than minutes. Contractors will be expected to show a written plan for summoning help and for keeping track of operators on site.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Several self-employed operators told the Journal they welcomed the changes but worried about the cost of reassessment. One, who works across the Marrow Sound, said: 'Most of us learned the hard way already. I'd rather they spent the money on decent radios for island jobs.'

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The board said existing tickets remain valid until their holders' reassessment date, and that axe work, handcart and hand-haul tasks are not covered by the new rules. Full guidance is available from accredited training centres.

units.title: Letters: thirty days, and other ambitions
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Sir, your report on the Kittering Holm clearance quotes a contractor saying that sixty to ninety days would be normal for a site of that size. I have run island clearances for twenty years and I would put it nearer the ninety. Good luck to the crew. They will need settled weather and a site lead who knows when to stop for the day. Name and address supplied, Tollinby.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Sir, every year your survey reports that axe handles cost exactly what they cost last year. Every year I pay more for them. Either your survey is buying from a better shop than I am, or someone is having a laugh. I would like the address of the shop. Name and address supplied, Weyhaven.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Sir, a small plea to clients who buy islands: please put a working radio mast on them before you send a crew. I lost two days on a job up the coast last spring because the only signal was on a rock you could reach at low tide. The rock was very nice. The phone call was not. Name and address supplied, Port Ammet.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast: today and tonight
units.author: met
units.text: Today: a frosty start inland, then dry and bright. Wind becoming light southerly. Maximum 10°C. Tonight: milder, with mist forming over the Sound after dark and thickening into fog patches by dawn. Minimum 6°C on the coast. Visibility moderate, becoming poor or very poor in places.

units.title: Tides: Gilliver
units.author: met
units.text: High water Gilliver 06:09 (4.4 m) and 18:31 (4.6 m). Low water 12:22 (0.6 m). Times are Sound Time. Spring tides: currents through the Lisle narrows and around the Holm landing will be stronger than usual for the next three days.

units.title: Notice to mariners: fog and sound signals
units.author: coast
units.text: With fog forecast over the Marrow Sound from tonight, mariners are reminded of their obligations under the collision regulations to proceed at a safe speed and to make the appropriate sound signals in restricted visibility. Small craft without radar should consider remaining in harbour. The Carrow Point fog signal is operational.

units.title: Inshore waters: Carrow Point to Weyhaven
units.author: met
units.text: Wind southerly 2 to 3, occasionally variable. Sea state smooth. Weather fair, becoming misty. Visibility good, becoming moderate this evening and poor or very poor in fog overnight. Outlook: fog persistent over the Sound for several days, slow to clear even by day.

units.title: Sound Lines: fog expected from tonight
units.author: ferry
units.text: With fog forecast from tonight, crossings on all routes will run at reduced speed and may arrive later than timetabled. Night crossings are most likely to be affected. We will post updates on this page. Please allow extra time for onward connections and listen for announcements at the terminals.

units.author: coast
units.text: Further to the earlier notice: temporary battery lamps have been placed at the foot of the Gilliver slipway during the hours of darkness. Four of the six permanent shore lights remain unlit pending replacement fittings. Vessels approaching in darkness or restricted visibility should continue to exercise caution.

units.author: power
units.text: The routine inspection at Brackwater substation continues today. Thermal survey complete; minor maintenance items have been noted for the winter programme. No interruptions are planned. Customers on the Gilliver feeder may notice a brief flicker at around 14:00 during switching.

units.author: council
units.text: Update for Rope Walk, Chandlers Row and the streets off the market square: until the replacement recycling vehicle is in service, collections will be made on Thursdays by a smaller van. The van may arrive later in the morning than the usual lorry. Please leave boxes out until collected.

units.author: council
units.text: Planning register update. Application ref. ADC/VEG/0917, Kittering Holm. Condition 3 (nesting bird check): discharged. Conditions 1, 2 and 4: details approved prior to commencement. Conditions 5 and 6: to be discharged on completion. No further applications have been received in respect of this site.

units.title: Gilliver Quay Row: supplies restored
units.author: power
units.text: Customers on Quay Row and the harbour front at Gilliver experienced a brief loss of supply at 14:03 during planned switching associated with the Brackwater substation inspection. Supplies were restored within four minutes. We apologise for the inconvenience. No further switching is planned today.

units.title: Libraries: new evening opening hours
units.author: council
units.text: From the start of next month, Port Ammet central library will open until 20:00 on weeknights. Branch library hours in Tollinby and Lisle are unchanged while the district library review takes place. The local history room keeps its existing hours: weekday mornings and Saturday afternoons.

units.author: coast
units.text: Further to the notice concerning works at Kittering Holm: controlled burning of timber is permitted at the island during the works. Smoke may at times be visible from the mainland and from vessels. Mariners and members of the public need not report smoke from the island during daylight unless flames are visible away from the landing area.

units.title: Fog advisory: Marrow Sound
units.author: met
units.text: Fog advisory, valid from 22:00 tonight until further notice. Dense fog patches are expected to form over the Marrow Sound and coastal fringes, with visibility below 200 m and locally below 50 m. Fog may persist through the day in places. Take care on coastal roads and allow extra time for crossings.

units.title: Sound Lines: late crossing running on time
units.author: ferry
units.text: The 19:30 departure from Port Ammet is running on time. Visibility on the Sound is currently moderate in mist. Later crossings tonight may be slower than timetabled as fog develops. Please listen for announcements on board and at the terminals.

units.title: Evening update
units.author: met
units.text: Mist is thickening over the Sound this evening, and the fog advisory comes into force from 22:00. Visibility at Carrow Point is currently 2 km and falling. Winds light southerly. Temperatures holding at 6 to 7°C on the coast. Fog likely to be slow to clear tomorrow.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Nov 1st. Tally this week, 230. First hard frost; the saws stuck in the cut of a morning till the men warmed them. Burrows played the fiddle Saturday and Mr. Hale danced with the broom. The dark comes early now. Men decline to work the north lines after four o'clock owing to the light going, which is only sense, and I have entered it so.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Nov 8th. Tally this week, 219. Supply boat late two days on account of fog, the men short of tobacco and in ill temper over it. Fog lay on the Holm all week so that we could not see the bunkhouse from the saw pit, which is not forty yards. The men called to one another all the day long to keep their places. Lamp oil, as before, more than allowed.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Middle watch, 21 Nov 1904. 00:00 Lamp burning well. Wind S 1, thick fog, visibility under a cable. Fog signal sounding from 23:10, two blasts every minute. 02:30 Engine for the signal checked, oil topped. 04:00 Relieved. Remarks: assistant keeper returned from Gilliver; his wife better.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Middle watch, 22 Nov 1904. 00:00 Lamp burning well. Fog continuing, visibility under a cable. Fog signal sounding throughout. 01:50 Answered a vessel's whistle to the south-west, not seen. 04:00 Relieved. Remarks: the fog makes the shore road invisible from the gallery, and the gallery invisible from the shore road. Both of us glad of the bell.

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Kittering Holm, 6 June. Mr. P. has relented at double rate, on condition that he fetches me each evening and returns each morning, and will not hear of my sleeping on the island. Landed at the old timber camp clearing, much overgrown. Goldcrests, coal tits, a treecreeper; a woodcock flushed from the bracken. Wood sorrel and wintergreen thick under the pines. [Sketch: wintergreen, flowering spike.]

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: 6 June, evening, Gilliver. A good first day. Note for tomorrow: the hazel and rowan along the landing path are well grown and unbrowsed to a height I should not expect on an island of this size, if there were deer. Have seen no tracks yet, but have not looked properly. Mr. P. arrived for me an hour before the agreed time and stood in the boat until I came.

units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Jan 22. Took Mr. Coyle over to the Holm with the slates, Father and me. Calm and grey. The curing sheds are at the landing with the salt store behind. We was done by three and Mr. Coyle very particular we was away before dark, though it was his slates and his sheds, and a good hour of light left. Paid 6s. Mother says I can keep one.

units.title: From the archive: Brackwater dam opened, 1968
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note: from the Courier of 19 September 1968, page 1. Our photographer that day also took a picture of the last cottage before the water reached it, which we did not print and still hold. 'The Brackwater reservoir was formally opened on Saturday. The valley, which has been filling since spring, now holds water enough, the engineer said, for the whole district for a generation.'

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: Our Gilliver Correspondent, January 1895. The woodmen are returned from the Holm, some weeks before they were looked for, and in poor spirits, the weather having been very severe and the work, we are told, unprofitable. They took the Saturday boat to Port Ammet without lingering in the village, which disappointed Mrs. Tull, who had laid in more candles.

units.title: LB-0302: Carrow Point fog signal, last staffed winter
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0302. Date: November 1979. Location: shore road below Carrow Point light. Kit: cassette recorder, external mic, no windshield. Duration: 44:20. Description: the old fog signal sounding two blasts every minute in thick fog; waves on the rocks; a car passing slowly at 21:40. Curator's note: the signal was replaced by an automatic horn the following year. Several listeners report that this file helps them sleep.

units.title: LB-0347: Tollinby market, cattle sale
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0347. Date: unknown, c. 1984. Location: Tollinby livestock market, sale ring. Kit: portable reel-to-reel, single mic. Duration: 27:05. Description: an auctioneer working at speed; cattle; a gate that squeals on every opening; laughter at 11:30 after an unrecorded remark. Donated by R. N. (Tollinby), who notes that 'the auctioneer was my cousin and nobody understood him either'.

units.title: Carrow Point Lighthouse
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Carrow Point Lighthouse stands on the headland at the western entrance to the Marrow Sound. It was first lit in 1871 and was staffed by a principal and an assistant keeper until 1980, when it was automated. Its character is four white flashes every twenty seconds. The keepers' logbooks from 1898 to 1931 survive in the society's holdings, with some gaps [citation needed].

units.title: Talk: Arnell notebooks
units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Before anyone builds anything on Miss Arnell's notebooks: she was on the Holm for days, not seasons, she was rowed out each morning and back each evening, and she was looking for birds. An absence of evidence collected between ten and five by a woman who disliked her boatman is not evidence of absence. I've read the whole notebook. It is charming and it is not a census.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project, tape 5: Mr. A. Rendle
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Q: You worked at the curing station as a boy? A: Two seasons. Gutting and salting, and carrying. Hard work but fair pay. Q: Did anyone ever stay on the island overnight? A: The foreman did, the first season. Second season he didn't. Q: Did he say why? A: He said the boat was cheaper than the hut. [laughs] That was the foreman. Everything was the price of something.
